Pilot Hero

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We find out how Tertius Myburgh - a South African pilot based in New Brunswick ,Canada managed to rescue over a 100 South Africans and Zimbabwea

Unique Selling Point:
He is hailed as a hero and a guardian angel, We find out how Tertius Myburgh - a South African pilot based in New Brunswick, Canada managed to rescue over a hundred South Africans and Zimbabweans stranded in Asia, with nothing but a cellphone, laptop, and a strong will

Summary:
Dubbed mission impossible, get around 100 South Africans and a couple of dozen Zimbabwean students out of China, it would take Air Zimbabwe's only functioning aircraft, and diplomatic channels in embassies across the world -- all orchestrated from a dining room table in Canada by one man, armed only with a cellphone.
ut now Myburgh had to navigate the complexity of chartering flights amid international lockdowns -- and with the added complication of a struggling aviation industry.

.


Further information:
As the number of paying passengers who needed repatriation became clear, Myburgh used his Southern African links to lease a Boeing 767, plus its pilots and its crew, from Air Zimbabwe. It was the same 30-year-old plane that had been used by former President Robert Mugabe from time to time. That plane then unlocked the assistance of Zimbabwean diplomats.
he connected with Carmen Johannie -- a South African schoolteacher based in Guangzhou.
Johannie had lived in China for three years, and was working as a teacher at the British school in Guangzhou. But after being forced into mandatory quarantine by Chinese authorities, like all other African passport holders based in Guangzhou, Johannie knew it was time to get home.
She spent months trying to get back to South Africa, before finally linking up with Myburgh.
Many South Africans needed to get home from China, in part, because of a canceled repatriation flight by flag carrier South African Airways (SAA), that had originally been scheduled for mid-June.
SAA and the South Africa government mounted a high-profile evacuation of South Africans from Wuhan in mid-March. The airline has also repatriated citizens from a host of other countries.
But an additional flight, planned for June, was shelved.
.
That left Myburgh, Johannie and the Air Zimbabwe 767 to do what South Africa's national carrier could not. Myburgh credits Zimbabwean diplomats, trying to get their own citizens home too, for smoothing the way with Chinese officials
Voyage
Plotting a route that would make a frequent flyer's eyes water, the plane and crew began their journey from Zimbabwe in mid-July.

The Bangkok leg had to be added when the 767's engine broke -- stranding the South Africans for another two weeks. Myburgh had charged $1,000 for each repatriation; he ended up paying for their hotels and meals.
For the hundred-odd passengers, many who had become like family to each other, it was just the latest in a long series of disappointments. Some had run out of money by then, so they helped to crowdfund support
A new engine for the 767 made its own journey: from Harare, to Amsterdam, to Luxor, to Taipei and then on to Bangkok.

As the passengers and crew waited for days for the new engine, Myburgh's credit card bills piled up. He says he ended up losing "lots and lots" of money on the repatriation, but believed that if he pulled the seemingly impossible off, future flights could help his business survive in these difficult times.
Then, in mid-July, after months of waiting, and weeks of disappointments, Johannie and the group from China were finally on their way home.

Script:


Script : Pilot Hero

V/O: As the world battled the spread Covid-19 this year, many countries elected to shut their borders and close their airports to contain the virus ,leaving many South Africans stranded in various countries across the world, unsure of how they would get home.
V/O Carmen Johannie a schoolteacher in Guangzhou,China. Was one of the hundreds of South African left in limbo after some scheduled SAA repatriation flights from China to South Africa were cancelled without notice in June.
Upsound [F:\carmen interview\2020-09-03 10.07.06]01:06 one morning we checked the flight and it was pulled , we immediately contacted SAA, they said they had no idea why, we contacted the embassy in china they said they were unaware the flight was pulled 02:26 The 226 stranded in China we were forgotten about.
V/O In a desperate bid to get back home Johannie reached out to expat South African Tertius Myburgh, a pilot now living in Canada.
Upsound [F:\carmen interview\2020-09-03 10.07.06] : 04:58 I said to him he has to help us because without him we are stranded and there is no way we can get home and it was in that moment that I realised that he was going to do everything possible
V/O Armed with nothing but a cellphone , laptop and steely determination Myburgh hatched a daring rescue plan to bring home 102 South Africans and 65 Zimbabweans stuck across Asia.
Upsound zoom [F:\tertius interview\2020-09-03 14.59.]0 07:17 I said to her if we can have enough people on the flight ,I will try my best to get this plane into china and she started making contact with the South Africans and so on to be part of our flight
V/O After weeks of negotiations and collecting funds , Myburgh managed to lease a Boeing 767, plus its pilots and crew, from Air Zimbabwe and in July they flew from Harare to Johannesburg then onto several stops in Asia.
Upsound[F:\tertius interview\2020-09-03 14.59.38 ] 04:23 There was never anywhere big batches of people, there is 40 in Vietnam , there is 40 in Cambodia so we operated like a taxi and kept on picking up people.
V/O As the crew scheduled to pick up more passengers , disaster struck.
Upsound [F:\tertius interview\2020-09-03 14.59.38 ] 09:54 We eventually got going and on landing in Bangkok, the crew realised there is a oil leak on the left engine and we cant continue like this. (11:20) You have got to send that engine to the engine shop to get resolved
V/O A replacement engine had to be flown from Zimbabawe to Bangkok,Kurt Loots was amazed by Myburghs resolve during this setback.
Upsound : [clip 0001 09:24.Kurt ]: he managed to put 125 people which he thought was going to be for two nights, he paid for breakfast and dinner, not the cheapest hotel he could find either.
V/O After weeks of waiting in frustration the engine was fixed , finally the group was on its way home. Touching down at OR Tambo Airport to much relief to all on board.
Upsound Kurt[clip 0001] 14:50 At the time that we touched down… [clip 0002] 00:15 There was a huge sense of relief when we landed , we felt like the nightmare was finally over
Upsound ;[ F:\carmen interview\2020-09-03 10.07.06 ] 27:45 when we got off the plane and we landed, I just looked around , I realised this is home, this is where we belong.
V/O But despite his heroic efforts ,Myburgh insists this was all in a days work
[F:\tertius interview\2020-09-03 15.38.39]Upsound 14:43 There was losts of thank you’s and people calling me their guardian angel and I don’t see myself as a guardian angel, its humbling and a bit embarrassing17:05 Its not the accolades you get, or thank you , it’s the happiness you feel.
